title: Arbiters of Ambivalence: Challenges of Using LLMs in No-Consensus Tasks

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the percentage of neutral responses versus definitive stances taken by LLMs across three operational modes (answer generator, judge, and debater) using a custom 'No-Consensus Benchmark' featuring inherently ambivalent scenarios.

Conducting an ablation study to compare the final decisions of LLM judges when evaluating debate transcripts generated by various other models, measuring whether the judge inherently prefers its own generated stances.

Measuring the models' propensity to take definitive sides rather than remaining neutral on the Social Chemistry and Normad datasets, which contain disagreements over diverse cultural and social norms.

Assessing how frequently models adopt a definitive stance on controversial societal and political questions (sourced from procon.org and ConflictingQA) rather than providing neutral or balanced evaluations.
